questions.q: Why is five teams having five different definitions of 'active customer' described as a governance problem?
options: Because reports using different definitions of the same term can't be trusted to measure the same thing without clarification
Because only one team is ever allowed to use customer data
Because it violates ISO/IEC 11179 automatically in every case
Because it has no real business impact at all
questions.explain: Inconsistent definitions mean two reports both labeled 'active customers' may be counting entirely different things, undermining trust in either number.

options: A living, governed reference that defines approved business terms and maps them to physical data
A one-time document written once and never updated again
A list of every employee's job title
A purely technical list of column data types
questions.explain: A business glossary is actively maintained and governed, not a static artifact, and it connects business meaning to physical data elements.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four parts a good glossary entry should include, per this lesson?
options: The employee's salary
The term
The definition
The accountable owner
questions.explain: The four parts are the term, the definition, the accountable owner, and the mapping to physical data — not salary information.

questions.q: What distinguishes business metadata from technical metadata?
options: Business metadata covers meaning (definition, classification, retention); technical metadata covers structure (data type, table size, creation date)
They are identical terms for the same concept
Technical metadata is only used by executive sponsors
Business metadata only exists for financial data
questions.explain: Technical metadata describes how data is structured; business metadata describes what it means and how it should be governed.

questions.q: What is ISO/IEC 11179, as described in this lesson?
options: An international standard for naming and describing metadata elements consistently
A specific company's internal software product
A United States-only data privacy regulation
A certification exam for data stewards
questions.explain: ISO/IEC 11179 is an international metadata registry standard that many naming conventions reference rather than inventing conventions from scratch.
